Long Description: Sales credit is a value assigned to a client trade that quantifies how much recognition the salesperson who executed the trade should get as a result of the transaction. Historically there have been standard sales credit rates applied to transactions depending on the product. Recently there has been a change to the sales credit policy within the FID Trading & Sales Business Unit to a concept of Economic Value (EV). EV uses profitability of trades to drive what the appropriate sales credit should be. Given this, there has been a push from the Trading & Sales BU to remove the legacy sales credit tables in TW and have assignment of sales credit be the responsibility of the trader. As a result, TC will not be required to assign sales credit for FID Client side trades. If a trade is worthy of sales credit, the Sales Credit Rate and Code will come down from upstream (risk system or BigMAC) into TC.
